clue.text: If rest is disturbed there's animosity

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order, so these six get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone woken from their sleep turns hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter conflict and hostility between people is a synonym for ill feeling.

clue.text: Singer failing to hold a note… -raising a laugh

indicators.note: the jumbled word holds the note inside it
a singer failing falls apart, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A vocalist who misses a note gets the audience giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges SINGER to SNIGER, and 'to hold' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly suppressed laugh is a snigger.

definitions.meaning: to retail a story is to recount or report it
selling goods in a shop to the public

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporting in store' looks like turning up for a shift; it is two senses, telling a tale and shopkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailing a rumour is telling it; retailing goods is selling them to the public.

definitions.meaning: fine-ish, quite splendid, written as FIN plus ISH

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as FIN-ISH, read as 'fine-ish', with ISH the suffix meaning rather.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine-ish means fairly splendid; the word also means a conclusion or close.

parts.note: the paper is not writing paper but manuscript paper for musical notes: an original piece written out there has been created by a composer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Note-paper' suggests letters; the notes are musical ones, and the clue describes a piece of music being written for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer who writes an original piece of music is said to have made it up on the stave.

clue.text: A stone circle to be seen with a friend

parts.note: O is the shape of a circle
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Ancient standing stones visited with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone circle' reads as a monument such as Stonehenge; split it, so 'stone' defines and 'circle' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone with iridescent colours.

definitions.meaning: British slang for prison or time in prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' reads as an instruction to mix the oats; it is British slang for prison, and doing porridge means serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a jail term; also a dish of oats cooked in milk or water.

clue.text: A dance where some university men turned on another

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: MAs, Masters of Arts, are university graduates
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is another university man

explanation.surface: University men twirl partners at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses MAS to SAM, and 'on another' adds BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Brazilian ballroom dance.

indicators.note: redesigning means laying out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A landscaper warns about the hazards of a garden makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Perils and hazards are threats.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A well-liked clergyman's architectural plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a clergyman, but here it is the verb, to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something can mean to plan or mean it, as in purpose.

clue.text: The turnover of many an essential food supplier

definitions.text: The turnover of many an essential food supplier

parts.words: The turnover of many an essential food supplier
parts.note: turnover here is a trader's sales; the essential food is milk, sold by the person who runs a milk business

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' tempts you to reverse something, perhaps 'many an'; it is the business sense, the volume sold by a supplier of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells or produces milk and cream is a supplier of a staple food.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from unfriendly' reads as 'very friendly'; 'from' is only a link between two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote in space, and aloof or reserved in manner.

parts.note: to win something is to gain it
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: A candidate collects backing in the face of resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay a claim is to deny or contradict it, so the past form means contradicted.

indicators.note: the word in says the letter for one sits within the word for business

parts.note: trade means business or commerce
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A businessperson suffers insults at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' opens the clue and looks like a plain preposition, but it places I inside TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is verbal abuse.

indicators.note: inside says the word for everyone sits within the word for declined

parts.note: to die is to decline or fade away
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Children who just played as the whole group stayed in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to toy or play idly.

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
in means inside

explanation.surface: Locking up armed men proves a feeble policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' is only a link here; 'wet' is a noun, as in 'out in the wet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather, the wet, is precipitation falling from clouds.

clue.text: Criminals-exerting squeeze, finding foreigners carrying cash

indicators.note: foreigners carrying cash have it held inside them, so one word holds the other

parts.note: strangers are outsiders or foreigners
L stands for pound, libra, a unit of cash

explanation.surface: Criminals strong-arming tourists who are carrying money.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers who choke their victims by the throat are murderers who apply pressure.

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Acting irrationally, without any thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreasonable' is in the sense of a price, too high.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreasonable price is a costly one.

parts.note: 26 down is LEAD, and the lead in a show is the star
a tout solicits custom

explanation.surface: The lead lawyer begins legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer, and 'proceedings' like a lawsuit; a tout is one who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off or begin is to get things going.

clue.text: On the square? That makes the lag grin!

indicators.note: the answer's letters, rearranged, make the phrase that follows, so this is an anagram

explanation.surface: Being honest at last brings a smile to the convict's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the square' sounds like honest dealing; it is the corner of a geometric square. The answer's letters jumbled give THE LAG GRIN, a lag being a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Each corner of a square is a ninety-degree corner.

clue.text: Answer for ships' officers in. the customary procedure

indicators.note: in says the officers go inside the word for procedure

parts.note: a rite is a customary ceremony or procedure
POs are petty officers in the navy

explanation.surface: A reply on behalf of naval officers following protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort or quick reply.

clue.text: 30, a little chap selected for promotion.

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small man gets picked to move up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for promotion' as the definition, but an apse is no promotion; the definition is 30, RECESS, since an apse is a recess in a church, and 'for promotion' only finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted alcove at the end of a church, a type of recess.

parts.note: E stands for east, oriental
to merge is to combine or associate

explanation.surface: A firm dismisses its eastern partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharges' reads as sacks; it is comes out, as a river issues forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Comes out or issues forth.

explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit or collide; and a walkout by employees.

indicators.note: the word for muggins is turned round, read right to left

parts.note: a muggins is a fool or sap
to sample something is to try it

explanation.surface: A fool goes back for another taste of the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry can be a single cake or tart.

clue.text: Petition about very quiet music man

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: to sue is to petition
pp, pianissimo, is very quiet in music

explanation.surface: A request concerning a very soft-spoken musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of light operas, best known for the Light Cavalry overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé was a nineteenth-century composer, a musician.

clue.text: Just a few words might well. be fine

definitions.meaning: a short complete grammatical unit of a few words
a court's penalty, such as a fine, is a punishment handed down by a judge

explanation.surface: A brief remark may be perfectly adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as 'all right'; it is the penalty a judge imposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, a short complete statement; legally, the punishment a court pronounces.

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The key agreement has been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead story or item is the principal one.

clue.text: He. fancies a little drink before the puzzle

parts.note: a sup is a small mouthful of drink
a poser is a puzzle

explanation.surface: A man likes a nip before tackling the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: One who supposes imagines or believes things, so he fancies.

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endless says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry about interminable drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final E of 'Imagine' to leave IMAGIN; 'confounded' rearranges those letters. 'training' is the sense of pointing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing a weapon at a target, as in training a gun on it.

clue.text: It's late in the day, for a regular course

parts.note: even means regular or uniform
a tide is a course or current, as in the tide of events

explanation.surface: An evening class keeps a steady schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: 20 writing about the Church with some craft

parts.note: re means about or concerning
CE is the Church of England
SS, steamships, is plural, some craft or vessels

explanation.surface: An essay on the Church and some of its boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 20, APSE; an apse is a recess. 'writing' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular alcove, a type of recess in a church wall.
